queries: WITH per_tif AS (SELECT o.timespan AS time_in_force, COUNT(DISTINCT o.recordvault) AS order_count FROM orders o JOIN riskandmargin r ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.timespan), shares AS (SELECT time_in_force, order_count, order_count * 1.0 / SUM(order_count) OVER () AS share FROM per_tif) SELECT time_in_force, order_count, share, share - AVG(share) OVER () AS diff_from_avg_share FROM shares

assumptions.assumption: Distinct orders are counted by orders.recordvault (the unique order reference used in the join), not orderspivot.

Orders with a NULL timespan form their own group (NULL time-in-force) and are included in the total and the average share, since the request says 'across the time-in-force values' and NULL is not excluded.
Share is a fraction (0-1) rather than a percentage; difference from the average share is share minus the mean of shares across the groups shown.

alternatives.interpretation: Exclude orders with NULL timespan, so only real time-in-force values count toward the total and average.

assumptions.assumption: Orders are identified by orders.recordvault (the unique order reference that riskandmargin links to), so distinct orders are counted by recordvault.

Share is a fraction (0-1) of the total distinct matched orders across all time-in-force values, and the difference is share minus the simple average share across the time-in-force groups (not a percentage).
Orders with NULL timespan form their own group, since the request says to show each time-in-force value and drop only unmatched records.

assumptions.assumption: Orders are identified by recordvault (the unique order reference that riskandmargin references), so distinct orders are counted by recordvault.
Only time-in-force values that have at least one matched risk/margin record appear; values with no matches are not listed and do not count toward the average share.
Orders with a NULL timespan, if any matched, form their own group and are treated as a time-in-force value in the share and average calculations.
'Difference from the average share' is the signed difference (share minus the mean share across the groups), expressed as a fraction, not a percentage.

alternatives.interpretation: Include every time-in-force value present in orders, even those with zero matched risk/margin records (count 0), so the average share is taken over all values.
